prs.title: [compiler] Preserve AST source offsets and declarator ranges
prs.author: magic-akari
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve original source offsets and declarator ranges when React Compiler rebuilds AST nodes in both Rust and TypeScript, so downstream AST consumers can identify the correct source ranges.

Generated nodes can retain `loc` while losing node-level `start` / `end` offsets. Declarator ranges derived from transformed children can become reversed after constant propagation or exclude the closing parenthesis of a cast initializer.

This change:

- Carries raw AST offsets through Rust lowering and codegen independently of `loc.start.index` / `loc.end.index`, storing them as internal, non-serialized HIR metadata.
- Restores TypeScript node offsets from the original AST during codegen.
- Carries statement and declarator locations separately in the existing instruction and instruction-value fields, then emits the original declarator range. Absent source metadata stays absent.
- Adds shared declaration-range assertions to snap, unit coverage for missing and shifted metadata, and `cargo test --workspace` to the Rust compiler CI workflow.

### Related
- vercel/next.js#97392
- web-infra-dev/rspack#15350

## How did you test this change?

- `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace`: 59 tests passed.
- Targeted Jest run for `CodegenReactiveFunction-test.ts`: 3 tests passed, including shifted and absent raw offsets.
- `yarn snap` and `yarn snap --rust`: 1,832 fixtures passed in each backend. The five `source-locations/` fixtures automatically assert original declaration ranges
…(truncated)

prs.title: [Fizz] Preserve the external runtime configuration when resuming
prs.author: eps1lon
prs.body:
## Summary

Resuming a prerender with an empty HTML shell can emit external-runtime instructions without loading the runtime that processes them. The postponed state preserves the data streaming format, but the runtime URL and integrity metadata were only kept in the original render state. This leaves completed Suspense content hidden when no shell was flushed before postponing.

Preserve the external runtime configuration in resumable state and restore it when creating the resumed render state. Existing resource deduplication prevents emitting the runtime again when it was already included in the shell.

## How did you test this change?

- added test (first commit for prior behavior)

prs.title: [Fiber] Ping a throttled retry when a new render cancels its timeout
prs.author: acdlite
prs.body:
When a retry finishes rendering and its commit is throttled, its lanes are marked suspended and the finished work is held behind a timeout. If another render starts before the timeout fires, prepareFreshStack cancels the timeout and throws that work away. The retry's data has already resolved, so nothing pings it again. Its lanes stay suspended until some other work commits. If the render that interrupted it keeps suspending, the retry never runs again.

This is how a transition gets stuck after giving up hydrating a dehydrated boundary (#38029). The same thing happens on the client when an unrelated transition interrupts a throttled retry and then suspends again: the boundary stays on its fallback until that transition's data arrives, or forever if it never does.

Fix this by pinging the throttled lanes when prepareFreshStack cancels the timeout, so the retry renders again once the interrupting render finishes or suspends. This also covers the hydration case, so the earlier fix in #38030 (pingSuspendedRetryLanes in updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent and updateDehydratedActivityComponent) is not needed.

Adds ReactSuspenseThrottledRetry-test.js with two cases: the interrupting transition commits, and it suspends again. The second fails without this change. The two hydration tests from #38030 are kept.

Fixes https://github.com/react/react/issues/38029
Closes https://github.com/react/react/pull/38030

Co-Authored-By: Hamidreza Hanafi <hamid_r_hanafi@yahoo.com>

prs.title: Fix crash when a deleted hidden Activity's suspended data resolves
prs.author: jackpope
prs.body:
When a component inside a hidden Activity suspends and there's no Suspense boundary in between, the Activity's Offscreen fiber acts as the suspense handler. At commit, `attachSuspenseRetryListeners` binds `resolveRetryWakeable` to that Offscreen fiber and attaches it to the thenable.

If the Activity is deleted before the thenable settles, it nulls out the Offscreen fiber's `stateNode`. There's no way to remove a listener from a promise, so when the thenable later resolves or rejects, the retry still runs against the detached fiber.

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_retryCache')

Because this runs inside a promise callback, it surfaces as an unhandled error rather than something an error boundary can catch.

The Suspense and SuspenseList branches of `resolveRetryWakeable` already treat a null `stateNode` as "no retry cache", and `markUpdateLaneFromFiberToRoot` already null-checks a deleted Offscreen instance (#24734).

Several apps have hit this in production and worked around it in userland: cevi/conveniat-webpage#1471, ACM-VIT/ExamCooker#460, remotion-dev/remotion#12303.

Added a regression test to `ActivitySuspense-test.js` that renders a hidden Activity around a suspending child, deletes it, then resolves the data. It throws without the fix.

prs.title: [DevTools] Keep unmatched console specifiers literal in single-string formatter
prs.author: hoxyq
prs.body:
formatConsoleArgumentsToSingleString builds the message key for errors and warnings logged during render, commit and passive effects. Its replace callback always shifted an argument, even when none were left or when the specifier was escaped (%%s). With no argument left, a specifier became 'undefined' or 'NaN', so '%s %s' with one argument gave 'value undefined' and '%d %d' with one argument gave '1 NaN'. An escaped specifier also shifted an argument, coerced it and put it back, so '%%d %s' with 'abc' gave '%d NaN', and '%s %%s' with one argument appended ' undefined'.

Leave a specifier as is when it is escaped or when no argument is left, like the browser console, Node's util.format and the sibling formatConsoleArguments helper (fixed in #36930) already do.

Fixes #37126

prs.title: [DevTools] Normalize BigInt values in facade inspection results
prs.author: hoxyq
prs.body:
The facade's normalizeValue() is documented to turn props and hook values into a serialization-safe shape, and it does so for undefined, functions, symbols, React elements and objects. BigInt fell through to the final `return val`, so getComponentByUid() returned raw BigInts in props and hook values. JSON.stringify() throws on BigInt, so consumers that serialize the result (such as the CDT MCP integration) failed to inspect any component holding one.

Convert BigInt to its decimal string with an "n" suffix, the same format DevTools uses for BigInt previews elsewhere. A string keeps the full precision (converting to Number would not) and the suffix keeps it distinguishable from a plain number or string. Only the normalized output changes; the application's values are not touched.

Fixes #37602

prs.title: [DevTools] Find non-resource hoistable instances in the facade
prs.author: hoxyq
prs.body:
getComponentByHostInstance reported React-managed <title>, <meta> and non-resource <link> elements as "not managed by React", even though the same fibers show up in getComponentTree and resolve by uid.

The facade's getHostInstanceForFiber only read a HostHoistable's DOM node from memoizedState.instance, which is where Resources (e.g. <style precedence>, <link rel="stylesheet" precedence>) keep it. Hoistables that aren't Resources have a null memoizedState and keep their instance on stateNode, the same as a HostComponent (see updateHostHoistable and the HostHoistable mutation path in the reconciler), so findByHostInstance could never match them.

Return stateNode when the hoistable has no Resource, and keep reading the Resource's instance otherwise. Add tests for both kinds.

Fixes #37604
